items.title: Decision entries do not carry the promised timestamps
items.statement: The purpose says every entry is timestamped and final, but the authoritative entry headings and PlanUnits expose identifiers and accepted status without any timestamp or finalization event. The excerpt therefore supplies no ordering, correction, or finality oracle for concurrent or superseding decisions.
items.impact: Consumers cannot deterministically order decisions, establish when a decision became final, or distinguish a later correction from an earlier entry.
items.builder_discretion: Define immutable decision timestamps, ordering/tie-break rules, and an explicit supersession/finality record rather than deriving order from file position.

evidence.exact_quote: Records decisions made during plan document updates that are not captured in `Plans/auto_decisions.jsonl` or `Plans/Decision_Policy.md`. Each entry is timestamped and final.

items.title: Owner and consumer authority is not adjudicated
items.statement: Decision_Log is declared owner for preserved behavior while cross-document ownership is delegated to ContractRefs and boundary notes. No precedence rule resolves disagreement between this ledger and a referenced owner, and no exhaustive consumer list or conformance obligation is provided.
items.impact: Two canonical-looking sources can disagree, and unlisted consumers can silently retain stale semantics.
items.builder_discretion: Specify per-decision normative owner, consumer inventory, precedence, and a machine-checkable conflict rule.

evidence.exact_quote: This source-preserving standardization keeps the owner and consumer boundaries stated in the original document body. During this batch, `Plans/Decision_Log.md` remains the owner doc for the behavior described by its preserved sections, while cross-doc ownership follows the ContractRefs and boundary notes already present in the original text.

items.title: Completion states lack a transition machine
items.statement: The log distinguishes Locally Complete, Available to Seam, and Seam Complete, but does not define legal source and destination states, entry and exit guards, idempotency, rejection behavior, or how package completion interacts with promotion and revocation.
items.impact: Implementations may permit skipped stages, stale promotions, double transitions, or incompatible completion truth across runtime and GUI.
items.builder_discretion: Define a closed transition table with guards, authority, event identity, idempotency, and invalid-transition outcomes.

evidence.exact_quote: `Locally Complete`, `Available to Seam`, and `Seam Complete` remain distinct. Package completion alone is insufficient.

items.title: Runtime ownership omits concurrency and retry invariants
items.statement: Runtime owns readiness, blockers, transitions, retries, and dispatch, yet the log supplies no lease, compare-and-swap, sequence, deduplication, retry budget, stale-writer, or split-brain rule governing simultaneous overseer and worker activity.
items.impact: Duplicate dispatch, retry storms, lost blocker updates, or completion after revocation can corrupt graph truth.
items.builder_discretion: Require monotonic event sequencing, idempotency keys, ownership leases, retry ceilings, and deterministic conflict resolution.

evidence.exact_quote: `Package Overseer` and `Seam Overseer` are distinct governance roles. Runtime remains the canonical owner of readiness, blockers, transitions, retries, and dispatch.

items.title: Graph patch generation has no atomic failure or rollback contract
items.statement: Creating a new graph generation and preserving historical paths is stated, but there is no atomic commit boundary, partial-write handling, failed-patch state, rollback versus roll-forward policy, recovery after restart, or rule for in-flight nodes on the superseded generation.
items.impact: A partial patch can expose mixed generations, orphan work, or historical lineage that does not correspond to executable graph truth.
items.builder_discretion: Specify transactional generation publication, immutable prior generations, in-flight node fencing, failure states, and deterministic roll-forward or rollback.

evidence.exact_quote: Graph patching creates a new graph generation and preserves superseded historical paths as visible lineage.

items.title: Optional attempt identity permits approval ambiguity
items.statement: Blocked approval identity makes attempt_id optional and does not define authorization, expiry, revocation, replay protection, or behavior when multiple attempts share a blocked sequence. Execution-unit context refs are named but not constrained.
items.impact: An approval can be replayed against the wrong retry or execution context, potentially authorizing stale or unintended work.
items.builder_discretion: Bind approvals to immutable episode and attempt identities, actor authority, intended action, expiry, nonce, revocation, and consumed state.

evidence.exact_quote: Approval anchoring moves to canonical runtime identity: `run_id`, `node_id`, `blocked_sequence`, optional `attempt_id`, and execution-unit context refs supersede request-centric button copy, request-centric persistence language, and tier-boundary approval `CTA` framing in `Plans/human-in-the-loop.md` (`/human-in-the-loop.md`). Gate/evidence schema mismatch is a first-class governance defect, not just a tooling gap, and `/evidence` contracts must expose the defect as such.

items.title: Actor-envelope data lacks a privacy lifecycle
items.statement: The actor envelope includes authentication and account identity, effective provider selection, tool context, and PRD/account lineage, but no minimization, field classification, encryption, tenant isolation, access control, retention, deletion, export, or redaction rules are present.
items.impact: Sensitive provider, account, tool, and product-lineage data can be over-collected, retained indefinitely, exposed across actors, or leaked through replay and support surfaces.
items.builder_discretion: Define a field-level data classification and lifecycle with least privilege, tenant boundaries, encryption, retention/deletion, redaction, and audit access.

items.title: Two-of-three corroboration is vulnerable to correlated or hostile inputs
items.statement: The deterministic vote threshold does not require independent identities or evidence, define eligibility, deduplicate shared provenance, handle abstention and timeout, limit retries, or specify what happens when later evidence invalidates an accepted claim.
items.impact: One source can be counted twice, colluding or compromised agents can manufacture canonical truth, and unresolved votes can stall or oscillate governance.
items.builder_discretion: Bind votes to independent actors and provenance, require eligibility and quorum rules, deduplicate evidence ancestry, and define timeout, challenge, and revocation transitions.

evidence.exact_quote: Corroboration disagreement handling uses the `2-of-3` rule: `2-of-3` accepts a high-impact claim as `/canonical`, no `2-of-3` means a high-impact claim is not accepted as blocking or canonical truth, and credible lesser concerns still emit a non-blocking `/minor` advisory visible on the Orchestrator page.

items.title: Weak-integration UI has no stale or degraded truth model
items.statement: The Seams UI must summarize and group weak integration, and blocked states expose recovery context, but no loading, stale, disconnected, permission-denied, partially aggregated, empty, or unknown state is defined. There is also no freshness indicator or rule preventing a locally cached state from appearing canonical.
items.impact: Operators may promote or remediate based on incomplete or stale seam truth while the interface appears authoritative.
items.builder_discretion: Define explicit freshness, loading, partial, stale, offline, unauthorized, empty, and error states and disable destructive or promotive actions when truth is not current.

evidence.exact_quote: Weak integration is not just a badge. Seams UI must summarize weak integration visibly and group concerns under readable headings such as Wiring, Workflow, State, GUI, and Design. Package issues roll up to seam concerns only when they cross package-to-seam, `/seam/user-visible`, or user-visible boundaries or affect seam completion truth. `Locally Complete`, `Available to Seam`, and `Seam Complete` remain distinct from `Lane to Package`, `Package to Seam`, and `Seam Completion` promotion boundaries.

items.title: Provider and approval flows omit offline and network-loss behavior
items.statement: The shared provider runtime spans provider-backed turns and the approval model depends on runtime identity, yet the core defines no timeout, reconnect, queued action, cancellation, duplicate-response, late-response, or offline read-only behavior.
items.impact: Network loss can duplicate provider actions, lose approvals, leave blocked episodes indeterminate, or show a success state before durable acknowledgement.
items.builder_discretion: Specify request identity, durable acknowledgement, timeout and cancellation semantics, reconnect reconciliation, and explicit offline GUI behavior.

items.statement: Historical graph paths remain visible and weak-integration concerns roll up across package and seam boundaries, but there are no caps, pagination, archival tiers, compaction rules, query budgets, fan-out limits, or performance acceptance criteria.

items.title: Canonical labels lack accessibility and localization contracts
items.statement: A fixed set of user-facing labels and readable group headings is mandated, but the log does not define semantic roles, keyboard and screen-reader behavior, non-color status cues, focus after transitions, announcement of dynamic changes, localization keys, pluralization, text expansion, bidi, or whether exact English tokens must remain untranslated.

items.title: Lane cleanup has no destructive-action safeguard
items.statement: Cleanup can be immediate or deferred through retained state, but there is no preview, confirmation, authorization, dependency check, cancellation, archive-before-delete, undo window, receipt, or recovery behavior for partial cleanup.

items.title: Identity and alias migrations lack a cutover protocol
items.statement: The log requires moving from tier_id and request_id identity and retaining compatibility notes, while some labels remain aliases, but it does not define versioning, backfill, dual-read/write, old-record interpretation, mixed-version behavior, rollback, telemetry, or alias retirement.

dimension_assessments.summary: ContractRefs name some owners, but no exhaustive consumer inventory, propagation rule, or conformance enforcement exists.
Distinct completion, revocation, and reopen labels exist, but legal transitions, guards, and invalid-transition behavior are absent.
Runtime and decision finality lack ordering, lease, idempotency, stale-writer, and split-brain invariants.
Graph-generation publication and research-packet regeneration have no partial-publication or last-known-good contract.
Graph patching, cleanup, and regeneration do not define rollback, roll-forward, restart recovery, or reversible tombstones.
Some authority splits are explicit, but cross-document precedence and approval actor, attempt, expiry, and replay boundaries remain ambiguous.
Debug capture hygiene is recognized, but provider/account/tool lineage has no field-level lifecycle or access contract.
Corroboration and approval inputs lack independence, provenance, authorization, nonce, replay, and hostile-input rules.
Weak-integration display is required but freshness, partial, stale, offline, unauthorized, and error truth states are not.
Provider-backed turns and approvals have no timeout, durable acknowledgement, reconnect reconciliation, late-response, or offline GUI contract.
Visible historical paths and rolled-up concerns have no fan-out, paging, archival, compaction, storage, or latency bounds.
User-facing governance truth lacks semantic, keyboard, focus, screen-reader, dynamic-announcement, and non-color requirements.
Canonical English labels are not separated from localizable copy and lack expansion, pluralization, and bidi behavior.
Identity and alias migrations have compatibility notes but no versioned cutover, backfill, dual-read, rollback, or retirement protocol.
Blocked context exists, but durable timelines, correlation, structured errors, metrics, alerts, support exports, retention, and runbooks do not.
Lane cleanup lacks authority checks, preview, confirmation, dependency fencing, archive, undo, receipt, and partial-failure recovery.
Owner precedence is ambiguous, derived packet publication is unsafe, and referenced contracts cannot be verified within this blind window.
Generic migration and index validators do not falsify the risky runtime, recovery, security, migration, GUI, accessibility, or cleanup behaviors.
The authorized window cannot determine whether external ContractRefs close or contradict these gaps; that requires the later cross-document phase.
